figures.name: a sitting cat, facing left, tail on the ground
figures.how: I started from the familiar tangram-cat idea of a square turned to a diamond for the head with two small triangles as ears, then built a sitting body from the two large triangles plus the medium triangle as the shoulder, and laid the parallelogram as the tail. I worked out the vertex coordinates by hand on the integer grid and fitted the pieces to them with a small helper script.
figures.seen_before: yes: the sitting cat with a diamond head and triangle ears is a traditional tangram figure; this exact arrangement I composed myself but from memory of that type

figures.name: a sailboat with two sails
figures.how: First versions with the sails resting on the full hull merged into a shapeless blob, so I rebuilt the hull as a wider trapezoid from the five small pieces and split the two large triangles into two sails with a thin gap for the mast. It took four checks and looks.
figures.seen_before: yes: sailboats are a standard tangram subject in puzzle books, though I did not copy a specific one

figures.name: an arrow pointing right
figures.how: The two large triangles joined on a leg make a right-angled arrowhead, and the remaining five pieces tile a straight shaft one small-triangle leg thick. I worked it out geometrically before the first check, and it read correctly on the first look.
figures.seen_before: unsure: the arrow shape itself is a universal sign; I do not recall it as a specific traditional tangram figure
